data.name: Until I Have You
data.detailed_description:
Until I Have You, is a story-driven, fast-paced, retro-aesthetic platformer, engulfed in a Cyberpunk setting.

Driving you to the edge of your seat as you run n' gun through enemies, the game recounts a thrilling story of regret, love and corruption, in a city that’s gone haywire and just doesn't give a damn.

This is the story of the ARTIST, a talented assassin, who has worked many dirty jobs in a long and successful career. Finally heeding the pleadings of his wife, he has decided it's time to quit this ugly business and live a simple and peaceful life. However the ARTIST’s clients know he is irreplaceable, and are unwilling to allow the craftsman to hangup his tool belt. They send him this message by kidnapping his wife, Emily, and make it clear, retirement is not an option! The ARTIST is determined to get his wife back, and prepares himself for one last assignment. He understands to be successful he needs to go all out, and he procures a rare exoskeleton suit. Although this provides him with additional powers, it also can cause hallucinations and affect his judgment.

If you could save someone, how much of yourself would you be willing to sacrifice?


Features:
  • 12 Chapters of immersive story-telling
  • Beautifully pixelated environments
  • Fast paced action
  • Over 60 unique Enemies and 12 Boss Fights.
  • Rich and Diverse Settings (both in gameplay mechanisms and visuals)
  • Fully Voiced Dialogues
  • Gritty Cyberpunk Atmosphere
  • Keyboard & Controller Support

reviews.review:
[h3] 🎮UNTIL I HAVE YOU [/h3]

[code] [quote=Wendrex] # **UNTIL I HAVE YOU**

**Developer:** Wormwood Studios  
**Publisher:** Digital Tribe  
**Playtime:** 3.8 hours  
**Platform:** PC / Steam  
**Status:** 👍 **Recommended**

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

# 🎯 **When Style and Atmosphere Carry the Experience**

**Until I Have You** is one of those games that proves technical complexity isn't required to create a memorable identity.

Its combination of **2D action, cyberpunk aesthetics, noir-inspired storytelling, and a deliberately decaying atmosphere** creates something far more distinctive than its scope might suggest.

It isn't perfect, but it has something considerably harder to find: **personality**.

---

## ⚡ **Introduction**

**Until I Have You** understands something many indie games overlook: style can be part of the design itself.

Its retro-futuristic visuals, dark atmosphere, and action-oriented structure work together to create something that feels like an underground cyberpunk story brought to life.

It's compact, stylish, and focused.

Most importantly, **it knows exactly what it wants to be**.

---

# 🎮 **Gameplay — 8.2/10**

The gameplay combines **2D action, gunplay, movement, and progression through equipment and abilities**, creating an experience that demands constant attention.

Combat isn't simply about moving forward and shooting everything in sight. Positioning, enemy awareness, and using your available tools effectively all matter.

There is a satisfying rhythm to entering an area, quickly reading the situation, and deciding how to approach the encounter rather than blindly rushing ahead.

The structure shares some DNA with classic action side-scrollers, but the cyberpunk presentation and narrative focus give it a distinct personality.

Once you understand its rhythm, the combat becomes considerably more fluid and rewarding.

---

# 🔁 **Loop & Replayability — 7.8/10**

The core loop is straightforward:

**advance → fight enemies → use abilities/equipment → survive → uncover more of the story → move forward.**

What keeps it interesting is the interaction between action, progression, and narrative.

The game doesn't try to manufacture dozens of hours of content.

Instead, it focuses on delivering a **compact experience where atmosphere, progression, and storytelling provide the motivation to keep going**.

That also means replayability isn't its strongest selling point.

Players looking for a game designed around dozens of repeated runs may find better alternatives elsewhere.

For players who prefer focused indie campaigns with a strong identity, however, the approach works extremely well.

---

# 🎨 **Graphics & Immersion — 9/10**

This is arguably the game's strongest area.

**Until I Have You** features highly distinctive pixel art combined with a cyberpunk visual direction that effectively communicates decay, violence, and technology.

Rather than trying to hide its technical limitations, the game turns them into part of its visual language.

The environments, characters, lighting, and retro-futuristic aesthetic work together to create a consistently deteriorating world.

It's the kind of art direction where you can recognize the game almost immediately from a single screenshot.

**Visual identity: excellent.**

---

# 🔊 **Sound — 8.8/10**

The audio design complements the game's identity very effectively.

The soundtrack reinforces its dystopian science-fiction atmosphere, while sound effects give weight to combat and interactions.

The real strength comes from how well the audio works alongside the visuals.

It isn't simply background music — the sound design actively contributes to the tone of the world.

For an independent production, this balance between visuals and audio is one of its most successful aspects.

---

# 📈 **Difficulty — 8/10**

The difficulty requires adaptation.

Early encounters aren't simply reflex tests. They also teach the player to recognize patterns and understand how the available tools can be used.

The game rewards a more deliberate approach.

Trying to push forward without understanding enemy behavior can turn relatively manageable situations into unnecessary problems.

The difficulty works best when you accept the game's intended rhythm instead of treating it like a conventional shooter.

---

# ⚙️ **Performance — 9/10**

On PC, **Until I Have You** delivers a lightweight technical experience appropriate for its 2D design.

The format also lends itself well to responsive controls, which is especially important in a game built around combat and movement.

I didn't encounter any major technical problems that negatively affected my 3.8 hours of playtime.

More importantly, the technical presentation stays out of the way and allows the important elements to shine:

**control, pacing, and atmosphere.**

---

# 🆚 **Comparison**

### **Hotline Miami**
The comparison comes mainly from the intensity of encounters and the idea of learning through failure.

**Until I Have You**, however, takes a more narrative-driven and cyberpunk-oriented approach.

### **Katana ZERO**
Both combine 2D action, retro aesthetics, and a strong focus on atmosphere and storytelling.

The pacing and structure are different, but the same appreciation for style is evident.

### **Ruiner**
The strongest similarity is the cyberpunk setting and depiction of a violent, decaying futuristic society.

Until I Have You approaches those themes through a more compact and deliberately retro presentation.

---

# ⭐ **SCORE**

🎮 **Gameplay:** 8.2/10  
🎨 **Graphics:** 9/10  
🔊 **Sound:** 8.8/10  
⚙️ **Optimization:** 9/10  
🔁 **Replayability:** 7.8/10  

## 🏆 **Final Score: 8.5/10**

---

# ✅ **PROS**

✔️ Excellent visual identity  
✔️ Strong cyberpunk aesthetic  
✔️ Distinctive pixel art  
✔️ Convincing noir atmosphere  
✔️ Solid combination of combat and movement  
✔️ Strong integration between narrative and setting  
✔️ Soundtrack fits the world perfectly  
✔️ Focused and compact experience  
✔️ Low hardware requirements  

# ❌ **CONS**

❌ The compact campaign may disappoint players looking for dozens of hours  
❌ Replayability is limited compared with games specifically designed around repeated runs  
❌ The pacing takes some adjustment  
❌ Players who dislike retro or cyberpunk aesthetics may not connect with the presentation  

---

# 🏁 **CONCLUSION**

**Until I Have You is a game whose personality is far bigger than its scope.**

After **3.8 hours of playtime**, what stands out isn't the amount of content, but how consistently the game delivers on its core vision.

It knows exactly what it wants to be:

**a compact, stylish, dark 2D action game heavily influenced by cyberpunk aesthetics.**

And it works because its individual elements support one another.

The art creates the atmosphere.  
The music reinforces the setting.  
The combat keeps you engaged.  
The narrative gives you a reason to keep moving forward.

This isn't a game for players looking for an enormous open world or hundreds of hours of progression.

It's for players who appreciate **strong art direction, atmosphere, 2D action, and independent games with a genuine identity of their own**.

👍 **Recommended.**
